title: Oatmeal, regular or quick, made with milk, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Oatmeal is made from whole oat grains that can be rolled (regular) or finely cut (quick‑cooking). When prepared with milk and added fat, it becomes creamy and richer in flavor. Oatmeal is commonly enjoyed as a hearty breakfast or as a base for sweet and savory dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats have been cultivated for over 5,000 years and are one of the oldest grain crops.
Rolled, steel‑cut, and instant oats differ in particle size, which determines cooking time.
Cooking with milk boosts calcium and vitamin D content compared with water.
Adding fat (butter, oil, cream) improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and makes the dish more satiating.
Oats contain beta‑glucan, a soluble fiber that helps lower cholesterol.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucan
items.content: Beta‑glucan helps reduce LDL cholesterol and supports immune function.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides sustained energy and helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, pantothenic acid, and folate aid metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D from milk
items.content: Preparing with milk increases calcium and vitamin D, essential for bone health.

items.title: Beneficial fats when added
items.content: A modest amount of butter or plant oil enhances flavor and aids absorption of fat‑soluble nutrients.

items.title: Allergy to oats or milk
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to oat proteins or milk proteins and should avoid the product.

items.title: Higher calorie content with added fat
items.content: Fat increases the energy density, so portion size should be monitored, especially on weight‑control diets.

items.title: Presence of phytic acid
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or thorough cooking lowers its level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook oatmeal in milk, add a pinch of salt and a small amount of butter or oil. Top with fruit, berries, nuts, honey, or spices such as cinnamon and vanilla. Quick‑cooking oats are convenient in the microwave, while regular rolled oats need 5‑10 minutes of simmering.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry oats in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked oatmeal should be cooled and kept in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days.
